did_you_know.text: Did you know? While Joab and the entire army of Israel were besieging Rabbah, the city of the Ammonites, David remained in Jerusalem and did not go out with the army.
Did you know? In the evening, David got up from his bed, walked around on the roof of the king’s house, and saw a woman bathing; the text notes that she was very beautiful.
Did you know? The woman David saw was Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
Did you know? After Bathsheba came to David, she returned home; the text notes that she was purifying herself from her uncleanness.
Did you know? Bathsheba told David that she was pregnant, and as a result David summoned Uriah from the battle.
Did you know? David tried to persuade Uriah to return home, but Uriah refused to go down to his house while the ark of the covenant, Israel and Judah, and the soldiers were in the camp and the field.
Did you know? David sent the order for Uriah’s death by Uriah himself, without Uriah knowing the contents of the letter.
Did you know? Joab placed Uriah where he knew there were strong enemy warriors, and afterward the soldiers withdrew from him; other soldiers were also killed in the battle.

Did you know? Joab prepared the messenger in advance for David’s possible reaction and even mentioned the death of Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth, who was struck by a piece of a millstone thrown from a wall.

Did you know? After the period of mourning, David took Bathsheba as his wife, and she gave birth to a son; however, the text concludes by stating that what David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
